Move Done panes into the collapsed Recently done sidebar section after this many minutes.

Automatically close eligible Done panes. Set false to disable reaping entirely.
Move completed or inactive panes into the Settled sidebar section after this many days without activity.
Settle a pane when the work it is linked to finishes, such as its pull request merging or its ticket reaching Done.
Wait this many minutes after linked work first reads as finished before settling the pane, and settle only if it still reads finished and the pane stayed quiet.
Settle a pane that has had no activity for settle_after_days.
Settle a resumable pane whose agent read Done and stayed quiet, instead of leaving it running until reap_done_after_minutes closes it. A pane with no resume plan is left to reaping.
How long a Done pane has to stay quiet before auto_settle_done settles it.
How many minutes a settled pane stays live and editable before becoming read-only. Zero locks it immediately.
Stop resumable agent processes when their pane settles. Unsettling the pane resumes the stored agent session.

After a pane resumes into its native agent session, submit resume_nudge_message once so the agent continues its work. Skipped when the agent resumes blocked or already working, and when the pane holds a draft you typed.
The prompt nudge_resumed_agents submits to a resumed agent.

Nudge an unsettled agent pane after its status declaration is stale and its pane activity has also stayed quiet. Blocked panes, closing gates, human drafts, pending launches, and panes without a matching live agent runtime are skipped.

Quiet period before Herdr marks an unattended finished report with unreported child work stale. An agent that reports itself working keeps a 20-minute budget, and declared waits use their ETA plus grace.
Quiet period before Herdr marks a parent waiting on declared running subagents stale. Changed detection-buffer output and fresh reports restart this budget; input alone does not.
Minimum pane inactivity before the first stalled-agent nudge. Later nudges wait two and four times this interval.

Maximum prompts Herdr sends during one stale-status episode. Answering a nudge parks the episode rather than refilling it; the budget resets once the pane stays healthy for a full escalation cycle, or as soon as you type into it.
Maximum stalled-agent nudges sent to one pane without human input, across status reports and recovered episodes. Once reached, nudging stops until you type into that pane. Set to 0 for no cap.

keys.default: "Re-verify what you are working on now; do not answer from memory. If you have subagents, poll them and restart any that are stalled. If everything is still progressing, reply with one line: Progressing, plus the count and names of running subagents if any (e.g. Progressing, 2 subagents: build, review). If it is done or something changed, say so and continue."
keys.description: Plain-text prompt submitted to a stalled agent. It works without an agent-specific command or installed skill.

Expose the focused pane's cursor anchor to the outer terminal even when the pane requested `?25l`, so macOS native input methods keep tracking the candidate window when TUIs paint their own cursor (Claude Code, pi, codex, etc.). Default: false.  When the pane reports no cursor position, falls back to the pane's top-left so a stable IME anchor is always available.  Trade-off when enabled: an extra hardware cursor will be visible in the outer terminal for apps that hide the cursor without painting a replacement (vim normal mode, etc.). See #149.

Restrict `reveal_hidden_cursor_for_cjk_ime` to focused panes whose detected agent matches one of these names (case-insensitive). Empty list means apply to any focused pane. Unknown agent names are ignored; if the list contains no valid names, the reveal does not apply. Accepted names: pi, claude, codex, gemini, cursor, devin, cline, opencode, copilot, kimi, kiro, droid, amp, grok, hermes, kilo, qodercli, qoder, qwen, qwen-code, maki.
Cursor shape rendered for the IME anchor when `reveal_hidden_cursor_for_cjk_ime` is enabled.

While prefix mode is active, temporarily switch the host input source to an ASCII-capable mode so prefix commands are read as ASCII even when an IME is active, then restore the previous input source when prefix mode exits. On macOS this selects the ASCII-capable keyboard layout; on Windows it switches the IME to English (ASCII) input. Windows support is currently limited to the Korean IME; with an IME for any other language, the input source is left unchanged. macOS and Windows only; a no-op elsewhere and a best-effort no-op if the switch fails.
